claims.text: First-line to restore perfusion; balanced isotonic crystalloid preferred.
claims.quote: IV fluids are administered as the first-line intervention to restore perfusion. Balanced isotonic crystalloid is preferred
claims.locator: Treatment of Sepsis and Septic Shock › Perfusion restoration

claims.text: 1 L crystalloid rapidly at first; most need ≥ 30 mL/kg in the first 3 h.
claims.quote: Initially, 1 L of crystalloid is rapidly infused. Most patients require a minimum of 30 mL/kg in the first 3 hours
claims.locator: Treatment of Sepsis and Septic Shock › Perfusion restoration

claims.text: Goal = tissue reperfusion without pulmonary edema from fluid overload (not a set volume).
claims.quote: the goal of therapy is not to administer a specific volume of fluid but to achieve tissue reperfusion without causing pulmonary edema due to fluid overload
claims.locator: Treatment of Sepsis and Septic Shock › Perfusion restoration

claims.text: Albumin: little evidence of survival benefit; may be considered after large crystalloid volumes.
claims.quote: Some clinicians add albumin to the initial fluid bolus in patients with severe sepsis or septic shock; however, there is little evidence demonstrating increased survival benefit. However, its use may be considered in patients who have received large volumes of crystalloids.
claims.locator: Treatment of Sepsis and Septic Shock › Perfusion restoration

claims.text: Starch-based fluids (eg, hydroxyethyl starch) ↑mortality: don't use.
claims.quote: Starch-based fluids (eg, hydroxyethyl starch) are associated with increased mortality and should not be used
claims.locator: Treatment of Sepsis and Septic Shock › Perfusion restoration
